title: Dual medial axes in finite-dimensional normed spaces
summary: We study medial axes of nonempty closed sets in finite-dimensional real normed spaces whose norms are $C^1$ away from the origin. Using the differential of the norm, we define the dual $k$-medial axis by requiring the contact covectors associated with nearest points to have affine dimension at least $k-1$. In dimension $n$, we prove that this set is $(n-k+1)$-rectifiable for every $1\le k\le n+1$, and hence has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-k+1$. We give a direct geometric proof and characterize the dual medial axes through the superdifferential of the squared distance function, obtaining an alternative proof from a theorem of Alberti, Ambrosio, and Cannarsa on singularities of semiconvex functions. Under the additional assumption of strict convexity, the ordinary and dual medial axes coincide for $k=2,3$, yielding the corresponding rectifiability results for ordinary medial axes. For $k=4$, however, the ordinary rectifiability conclusion can fail even for norms arbitrarily close to Euclidean: we construct norms on $\mathbb R^3$ with smooth positively curved unit spheres arbitrarily $C^\infty$-close to the Euclidean sphere, together with four-point sets whose ordinary $4$-medial axes contain nondegenerate line segments.

title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
summary: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.

title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
summary: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
summary: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
summary: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.
